title: Anniversaries
tomorrow: why would anyone call your baptism day your first birthday?

segments.voice: Yesterday was birthdays, and a line you could say to someone across a cake: thank God for you. Today, the other days that come back every year.
screen: `THANK GOD FOR YOU.` → `THE DAYS THAT COME BACK.`

segments.voice: Your phone does it without asking: a photo from this day, years ago. The Bible has its own version, made of rocks. Israel is crossing the Jordan. The priests carrying the ark stand in the riverbed, and the whole people walk past them on dry ground. Then Joshua stops twelve men, one from each tribe, and tells each to lift a stone from the middle of the river and carry it out. Why haul rocks on the busiest day of your life?
screen: `A PHOTO FROM THIS DAY, YEARS AGO.` → `DRY GROUND IN THE JORDAN.` → `TWELVE STONES, CARRIED OUT.`

segments.voice: Because someday a kid will ask. In chapter four Joshua says it: when your children ask what these stones mean, tell them the river stopped for us here. The stones aren't for the people who crossed. They're for the ones who weren't there yet, so the day keeps teaching. Catholics fill the year with stones like that. A wedding anniversary, when a couple can ask for a blessing from the Church's book of blessings. An ordination anniversary, when a parish prays for its priest. A sister's or a brother's vow day. And the day someone died, often kept with a Mass offered for them. That last one leans on a line from Maccabees, in the Douay-Rheims: "It is therefore a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead, that they may be loosed from sins." One to tell a friend: the Church calls a saint's death day dies natalis, a birthday, the day they were born into heaven. And at the Last Supper, Jesus turned a meal into a remembering that never stops: "Do this for a commemoration of me." In the Bible, remembering isn't nostalgia. It hands the day to the people who come after.
screen: `WHAT MEAN THESE STONES?` · `WEDDINGS, ORDINATIONS, VOWS.` · `A MASS ON THE DAY THEY DIED.` · `DIES NATALIS — BORN INTO HEAVEN.` · then, large: `REMEMBERED DAYS.`

segments.voice: Find a pen and a calendar, paper or the one in your phone. Pick one date that belongs to someone: a wedding, a vow, a death. Write their name on it, slowly, by hand if you can, and stay with that name until the bell. If you pray, you can pray for them by name.
Anniversaries. Days that come back each year so the story keeps teaching: marriages, ordinations, vows, and deaths remembered. Today's word.
Keep this one: remembered days, stones carried out of the river for whoever asks next. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics often have a Mass offered for someone on the anniversary of their death; couples and priests may mark wedding and ordination anniversaries with a Mass or a blessing.
